div.span: Authorisation code flow with PKCE (S256), state and nonce. Scopes: openid, profile, offline_access
and Keyring's own API scope (api://<client ID>/access_as_user, or ENTRA_API_SCOPE).
The ID token is checked (signature, issuer, audience, expiry, nonce). The access token for Keyring's API
and the refresh token stay in the server's memory. Step-up adds acrs claims or prompt=login with max_age.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 626px; height: 1px; padding-top: 456px; margin-left: 28px;

div.b: 2. On-behalf-of exchange, per resource, cached per session until 5 minutes before expiry
div.span: https://vault.azure.net/.default Key Vault data plane
https://management.azure.com/.default ARM and Resource Graph (roles, PIM, diagnostic settings)
https://api.loganalytics.io/.default Log Analytics queries (audit pages, Used by, Keyring activity)
Grant: urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:jwt-bearer with requested_token_use=on_behalf_of.
Keyring authenticates the exchange with its client secret or the federated credential (right).

div.span: No client-credentials grant, app-only token or managed identity is ever used on this side.
Key Vault RBAC (or access policies) decides every request. Keyring's permission hints only grey out buttons.
PIM activation is a PUT to roleAssignmentScheduleRequests with the person's ARM token.

div.b: Platform only: Keyring's own config vault
div.span: App Service or Container Apps resolves Key Vault references at start. Role: Key Vault
Secrets User on the config vault (client secret, session secret). Keyring's code never calls it.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 606px; height: 1px; padding-top: 666px; margin-left: 728px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #1c222a;
display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#1c222a, #ccd1d8); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;
div.b: What the identity does not have
div.span: No role on any vault people use, on Resource Graph, or on any workspace's data.
It never reads KeyringAudit_CL: the audit page reads it as the person.
No access key, connection string, SMTP password or second identity.
The app registration holds delegated permissions only, so the federated credential gives
no vault access while nobody is signed in. Adding an application permission is a security change.
